availableTests: None required for initial dehydration classification
classificationRationale: Not lethargic or unconscious and not unable to drink.
clinicalTruth.diagnosis: Diarrhoea with dehydration requiring classification and rehydration plan
doNotDo: Do not prescribe only medicine without dehydration classification.
Do not send home before the 4-hour Plan B reassessment.
followUp: Counsel caregiver on fluids, feeding, and danger signs.

guidelineActions.action: Give ORS Plan B at 75 ml/kg over 4 hours: 750 ml over 4 hours for this 10 kg child.
guidelineActions.rationale: IMNCI Plan B applies to some dehydration.

guidelineActions.action: Give zinc 20 mg once daily for 10-14 days.
guidelineActions.rationale: The child is 18 months old, so the over-6-month zinc dose applies.

guidelineActions.action: Reassess after 4 hours and reclassify hydration status.
guidelineActions.rationale: Response to rehydration determines the next plan.

guidelineActions.action: Teach caregiver ORS mixing/use, continued feeding, and immediate return signs.
guidelineActions.rationale: Caregiver counseling is part of diarrhoea management.

medicines: Zinc 20 mg once daily for 10-14 days
clinicalTruth.referralThreshold: Severe dehydration, lethargy/unconsciousness, inability to drink, or shock require urgent referral or higher-level management.
reviewerQuestions: Confirm ORS Plan B volume and zinc duration used in current local practice.
